```{r setup}
library(CentralDogma)
```

## What is CentralDogma?

CentralDogma is a small package that follows the central dogma of molecular biology (DNA → RNA → protein). It lets you simulate a DNA sequence, convert it to RNA, split a sequence into codons, look up amino acids in the standard genetic code (the built-in dataset `codonList`, 64 codons), and plot how often each amino acid occurs.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
#install.packages("devtools") 
devtools::install_github("rforbiodatascience26/group_20_package")
```

## Functions

### Function 1 - DNA sequence generation

### Function 2 - DNA transcription

The `transcription()` function represents the transcription step of the central dogma of molecular biology. It takes a DNA sequence as input and converts it into an RNA sequence by replacing every thymine base (`T`) with uracil (`U`). The other bases remain unchanged.

### Function 3 - Codon generation

### Function 4 - Translation to amino acids

**`codonSelector(codons)`** takes integers (positions 1–64 in `codonList`) and returns the matching amino acids as one string.

```{r}
codonSelector(codons = c(1, 2, 3))
```

### Function 5 - Amino acid visualization

The function plot_aa_counts() takes an amino acid sequence written in one-letter code and returns a bar plot showing how many times each amino acid occurs in the sequence. This gives a quick overview of the composition of a protein or peptide. The output is a ggplot object, so the plot can be customised further with ggplot2, for example by adding a title or changing the axis labels.
